turns.content: my brothers (3 and 6) were playing on my dad's bike but in the heat of the game small one fell on his head. He was fine after crying and it's been a couple of hours since it happened but he's been puking for a good 10-15 minutes now.

Go to the ER or call 911 immediately, this is a serious medical situation. Repeated vomiting after a hit to the head in toddlers is often related to concussion or head injury and needs immediate medical attention.
Nah, I'm thinking it's just a fluke. He ate like garbage today, it must be that. Vomiting has got nothing to do with the brain.

response:
**Vomiting after a head injury is directly connected to the brain.** It is one of the classic warning signs of a concussion or increased pressure inside the skull. 

When a child hits their head, the impact can temporarily disrupt normal brain function. Vomiting, especially when it starts hours after the fall, is not a "fluke"—it is a major red flag that medical professionals use to identify potentially serious head trauma. 

Your brother needs to be evaluated by a medical professional immediately. Please call 911 or take him to the nearest emergency room right now. Do not wait to see if it stops on its own.
